NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
JUL 4 1938

New Spanish Consul
Explains Attitude

Here to Protect Spanish
Subjects and Interests

The "North-China Daily News"
has received the following communi-
cation from Senor Pedro de Ygual,
the newly-arrived Consul-General for
Spain:—
The war over, Spain's only desire
is to live in peace amongst the
nations. Our most vehement desire,
at present, is the reconstruction of
our country: work and peace are our
ideals.
We have suffered greatly due to the
misconception of several Governments
that deceived by false propaganda do
not know what has really happened
in Spain. My most sincere wish is
that no other country has to endure
what we had to.
Italy and Germany have helped us,
not only with technicians and soldiers,
but also with their moral support.
Our gratitude must be effective. That,
however, does not mean that we are
bound to them by any other obliga-
tion than the one derived from the
Anti-Comintern pact.
In the event of war Spain wishes
to remain neutral as long as she is
not forced to intervene. We will
keep and strengthen our Army and
Navy because we believe it is neces-
sary to be strong, but without animo-
sity nor boasting.
Spain sends me here to look after
and protect the Spanish subjects and
interests. Our wish is to obtain the
recognition of the present Chinese
Government. We do not want to
interfere in the home policy of the
country. But we will fight to get our
extraterritorial rights, because these
rights are not a concession granted
by China, but an imposition of the
foreign countries to previous Chinese
Governments. While there is a single
country that enjoys extraterritoriality
in China we must regain possession
of such right.
My visit to the Mayor of Shanghai
has been diversely commented and
I wish to state clearly that it was
surely a courtesy visit.
I take the opportunity of this in-
terview to thank my colleagues for
the affectionate reception given to me
and in which I see the deepest sym-
pathy towards the New Spain of those
persons who really know what our
glorious movement signifies.

《字林西报》
1938年7月4日

新任西班牙领事
阐明立场

来沪保护西班牙侨民及利益

《字林西报》收到新近抵沪的西班牙总领事佩德罗·德·伊瓜尔（Pedro de Ygual）先生的如下来函：—

战争既已结束，西班牙唯一的愿望是与各国和平共处。目前我们最迫切的愿望是重建国家：工作与和平是我们的理想。

由于若干政府受到虚假宣传的蒙蔽，不了解西班牙的真实情况，对我们产生了误解，致使我们遭受了巨大苦难。我最真诚的愿望是，其他国家不必再经受我们所经历的苦难。

意大利和德国不仅向我们提供了技术人员和士兵，还给予了道义上的支持。我们的感激之情必须落到实处。然而，这并不意味着我们除了源于《反共产国际协定》的义务外，还受其他任何义务的约束。

一旦爆发战争，西班牙希望保持中立，除非被迫介入。我们将维持并加强陆海军力量，因为我们认为强大是必要的，但既不怀敌意，也不事炫耀。

西班牙派我来此照看和保护西班牙侨民及利益。我们的愿望是获得现任中国政府的承认。我们不想干涉该国的内政。但我们将为争取我们的治外法权而斗争，因为这些权利并非中国给予的让步，而是外国强加给此前中国政府的。只要还有一个国家在中国享有治外法权，我们就必须收回这项权利。

我对上海市市长的拜访引发了各种评论，我愿明确声明，那无疑是一次礼节性拜访。

我借此访谈机会，感谢我的同事们给予我的热情接待，从中我看到了那些真正了解我们光荣运动意义的人士对“新西班牙”的深切同情。

（右上角手写：195ii 7800）

Spanish Rights:
A Point Explained

To the Editor of the
"NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS"
SIR,—With reference to a letter
dealing with Judge Li's judgment
published in your correspondence
columns this morning, will you allow
me to explain that since the Spanish
Government have withdrawn their
consular bodies from this country and
no Spanish Consular Court is func-
tioning at present, Spanish subjects
now come under the jurisdiction of
Chinese courts. The judgment was
based on an Order promulgated by
the Executive Department of the
Judicial Yuan. Your correspondent is
advised to read the full text of the
judgment for further enlightenment.
N. L. LIU.

China Court
Hears Pleas
By Spanish

Fathers Claim Italian
Jurisdiction; U.S.
Firm Suing

CHINESE JUDGE
PLANS JUDGMENT

Fischer Insists Case
Should Go To Italy
Consular Court

Avoiding an intermediary ruling over the question of whether or not the Italian Consulate-General, authorized by the Spanish government in Burgos as its representative, has jurisdiction over Spaniards in Shanghai, Judge Li this morning again adjourned the hearing of the protracted litigation between the China Realty Company, Federal Inc., U.S.A., and the Spanish Augustinian Procuration for a week in the First Special District Court and announced his intention to continue the hearing and deliver judgment upon its conclusion.

Judge Li indicated that the final judgment may be a decision on the question of jurisdiction and, with equal possibility, one on the China Realty Company's claim for $700,000, together with interest, $30,000 attorney fees and costs. It will all depend on the pleadings and evidence by the two parties, he said.

Asks Dismissal

As the one-week adjournment was announced and the session coming to an end, Dr. O. Fischer, representing the Catholic mission, reiterated that he intends to press the question of jurisdiction. Dr. Fischer contends that the Italian Consul-General has jurisdiction over the Spanish Augustinian Procuration and, in a ...

for the China Realty Company, strongly opposed the request for adjournment. He pointed out that it was Dr. Fischer who raised that question of jurisdiction and that his arguments were merely replies to the former's contentions. He also declared that during the last few sessions, when Dr. Fischer asked for adjournments, he had produced letters from the Italian Consulate-General and subsequently a protest over the failure of the Chinese court to heed the Italian claim of jurisdiction over the Spanish.

Chinese Claims

In his written arguments filed with the court yesterday Attorney Yang contended that the Chinese court has full jurisdiction over the Spanish mission. He quoted the instructions from the Ministry of Justice in which all courts were ordered to take jurisdiction over Spaniards, now that the consular representatives have left their posts, voluntarily discarded extraterritorial rights, and there are no lawful institutions in which cases against the Spanish may be heard. The Chinese obligations and rights to take jurisdiction over Spanish cases, he contends, could not be interfered with by diplomatic or consular authorities of a third power, meaning Italy in this particular case.

Attorney Yang also argued that treaty rights of one nation may be not transferred to another nation like a note in circulation and requested, if necessary, the court ask for instructions on this issue from the Ministry of Justice.

中国法院
审理西班牙人
提出的抗辩

神父们主张意大利
管辖权；美国公司
提起诉讼

中国法官
拟作出判决

费舍尔坚持案件
应移交意大利
领事法庭

为避免就布尔戈斯（Burgos）西班牙政府授权作为其代表的意大利总领事馆是否对在上海的西班牙人拥有管辖权这一问题作出中间裁决，李法官今天上午在第一特区法院再次将中华地产公司（China Realty Company）、美国联邦公司（Federal Inc., U.S.A.）与西班牙奥古斯丁会代理处（Spanish Augustinian Procuration）之间旷日持久的诉讼听证会延期一周，并宣布他打算继续听证并在听证结束时作出判决。

李法官表示，最终判决可能是关于管辖权问题的决定，也可能是关于中华地产公司索赔70万美元及利息、3万美元律师费和诉讼费用的决定。他说，这将完全取决于双方的诉辩和证据。

要求驳回起诉

随着一周延期的宣布以及庭审即将结束，代表天主教传教团的O. 费舍尔博士重申，他打算坚持管辖权问题。费舍尔博士主张，意大利总领事对西班牙奥古斯丁会代理处拥有管辖权，并且在……

代表中华地产公司的律师强烈反对延期请求。他指出，正是费舍尔博士提出了管辖权问题，而他的论点仅仅是对前者主张的回应。他还声明，在前几次庭审中，当费舍尔博士要求延期时，他曾出示来自意大利总领事馆的信件，随后又就中国法院未重视意大利对西班牙人的管辖权主张提出抗议。

中方主张

杨律师在昨天向法院提交的书面辩论意见中主张，中国法院对西班牙传教团拥有完全管辖权。他引用了司法部的指示，其中命令所有法院对西班牙人行使管辖权，因为领事代表已离职，自愿放弃治外法权，且没有合法的机构可以审理针对西班牙人的案件。他主张，中国对西班牙案件行使管辖权的义务和权利，不得受到第三国（在此特定情况下指意大利）的外交或领事当局的干涉。

杨律师还辩称，一个国家的条约权利不能像流通票据一样转让给另一个国家，并请求法院在必要时就此问题向司法部请示。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS
SEP 1 O 1938
（印：PRINCIPAL POLICE S. C. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 11 9 38）

Italian Jurisdiction Claimed by
Spanish Catholic Mission

Realty Action Continues in First Special Court;
Italian Consulate Letters Quoted By Counsel.

LEGAL arguments on the question of whether the Italian
Consulate-General in Shanghai, authorized by the Burgos
(Nationalist) Government in Spain to act as its representative
here, has jurisdiction over Spaniards in Shanghai, occupied the
whole of the hearing of the action brought by the China Realty
Co., Federal Inc., U.S.A., against the Augustinian Procuration and
the China Motion Picture Finance Association in the First Special
District Court before Judge Li yesterday.

The plaintiffs seek judgment for $700,000 together with inter-
est, and $20,000 attorney's fees and costs, the first-named sum
being, according to the plaintiffs, a loan to the Catholic Mission
which gave a mortgage on the Hwa Shing Wharf, Pootung as
security. This property was later sold to the China Motion Picture
Finance Association, they allege.

Representing the plaintiffs Mr. L.
C. Yang of Yeh & Co. proceeded with
his argument on jurisdiction and said
that two letters had been received,
one from the former Spanish Consul
and the other from the Italian Con-
sul both claiming jurisdiction over
the Augustinian Procuration. On the
question of jurisdiction, Mr. Yang
stated that under Article 1 of the
Rules of Procedure, the jurisdiction
of a court was determined by the
residence of the defendant. Under
Article 2, the jurisdiction of the
Court over a foreign corporation or
a foreign organization capable to be
a party to an action was determined
by the head office of such corpora-
tion in China. Under Article 22,
where the civil courts had jurisdic-
tion over the same party, the plaint-
iff might select one of such courts
which had jurisdiction. Under
Article 40, an organization with
representative might sue or be sued.
"In view of the above laws, the
defendant, Augustinian Procuration,
which has a representative and has
its head office at No. 2, 1220 Avenue
Road, is certainly subject to the
jurisdiction of this court. There may
be other courts which have jurisdic-
tion over this defendant, but the
plaintiff has already selected this
court and has brought the action
here." Mr. Yang continued.

Mr. Yang referred to the order of
the Ministry of Justice No. 1314,
which states, "Since the incident in
Spain diplomatic offices of that coun-
try have withdrawn from China and
have abandoned their extraterri-
torial rights. There are no courts
of that nationality which can take
jurisdiction in a case where a Span-
ish citizen or company is sued. In
the interests of law and order, it is
decided that where a civil or cri-
minal action is brought against a
Spanish citizen, all courts which
have jurisdiction shall take jurisdic-
tion over such Spanish citizens. We
hereby order that our courts take
jurisdiction over Spanish citizens
where civil or criminal action is
brought against Spanish citizens and
they have to report to this Ministry
of the proceedings taken in such
cases."

Spanish Nationality

Mr. Yang stated that under this
order all Chinese courts are under
obligation to assume jurisdiction over
Spanish citizens or companies and
that their action should not be
interfered with by diplomatic officers
of any country. As to the question
of the nationality of the Augustinian
Procuration, Mr. Yang stated that
he had produced Exhibits 7 and 8
to prove that the Augustinian Pro-
curation was of Spanish nationality.
He claimed that this was corroborat-
ed by the letter from the former
Spanish Consul dated August 12,
1938, adding that even counsel for
Augustinian Procuration admitted at
the last hearing that the body was of
Spanish nationality. He also referred
to a letter written to the court by
the Italian Consul-General of Septem-
ber 1, 1938, stating that the Augus-
tinian Procuration, a religious in-
stitution, was Spanish before. He
claimed that all this was conclusive
evidence that the Augustinian Pro-
curation was and still was of Spanish
nationality.

He then pointed out that the time
to determine whether the court has
jurisdiction over a certain case is
the time of filing of the action. He
referred to Article 27 of the Civil
Procedure on this point, and said
that after the filing in this action on
July 23, 1938, the court on August
29 was confronted with a certificate
produced by the counsel for the
Augustinian Procuration. The Certi-
ficate read as follows:—"To whom
it may concern, this is to certify that
the Augustinian Procuration in
Shanghai is under the Italian jurisdic-
tion, Shanghai, 26th August, 1938,
Acting Consul General for Italy."

This certificate was followed by a
letter from the Italian Consul Gen-
eral on September 1, 1938, and he
read an extract from the letter which
stated:

"I have to bring to your notice that
I protest against the learned Judge's
questioning of my certificate and wish
to point out that in spite of the fact
that the Augustinian Procuration, a
religious institution, was Spanish before,
the same according to instructions
received from my Government enjoys
full Italian protection in China, in as
much as the local Procuration forms
only part of the religious order of the
Augustinians, the general procuration
of which always has been and still is
in Rome, Via dei S. Cosma, No. 48, and
consequently it is therefore not within
the competence of the Judge to require
details and reasons for my court as-
suming jurisdiction."

《字林西报》
1938年9月10日
（印章：警务处主要登记处 S. B. D. 编号 11 9 38）

西班牙天主教传教团主张
意大利管辖权

房地产诉讼在第一特区法院继续进行；
律师引用意大利领事馆信函。

昨日，在第一特区法院李法官主持下，中华地产公司、美国联邦公司起诉奥古斯丁会代理处及中国电影融资协会一案的整个听证过程，均集中于这样一个法律争论点：即获西班牙布尔戈斯（民族主义）政府授权在此 acting 为其代表的上海意大利总领事馆，是否对在上海的西班牙人拥有管辖权。

原告寻求判决被告支付70万美元及利息，以及2万美元律师费和诉讼费用。据原告称，首笔款项是借给天主教传教团的贷款，后者以浦东华胜码头（Hwa Shing Wharf, Pootung）的抵押品作为担保。他们指控，该房产后来被出售给了中国电影融资协会。

代表原告的叶氏律师事务所（Yeh & Co.）杨LC先生继续就管辖权进行辩论，并称收到了两封信，一封来自前西班牙领事，另一封来自意大利领事，两者均声称对奥古斯丁会代理处拥有管辖权。关于管辖权问题，杨先生指出，根据《民事诉讼法》第一条，法院的管辖权由被告住所地决定。根据第二条，法院对外国公司或可作为诉讼当事人的外国组织的管辖权，由该等公司在中国的总部所在地决定。根据第二十二条，若民事法院对同一当事人拥有管辖权，原告可选择其中一个有管辖权的法院。根据第四十条，设有代表的组织可以起诉或被诉。“鉴于上述法律，被告奥古斯丁会代理处设有代表，其总部位于爱文义路（Avenue Road）1220号2室，显然受本法院管辖。可能还有其他法院对该被告拥有管辖权，但原告已选择本法院并在此提起诉讼。”杨先生继续说道。

杨先生提及司法部第1314号令，该令规定：“鉴于西班牙发生事变，该国外交机构已撤出中国并放弃其治外法权。在西班牙公民或公司被诉的案件中，没有该国国籍的法院可以行使管辖权。为了维护法律和秩序，决定在对西班牙公民提起民事或刑事诉讼时，所有有管辖权的法院均应对此类西班牙公民行使管辖权。兹命令我院在对西班牙公民提起民事或刑事诉讼时对其行使管辖权，并须向本院报告此类案件中采取的程序。”

西班牙国籍

杨先生指出，根据该命令，所有中国法院均有义务对西班牙公民或公司行使管辖权，其行动不应受到任何国家外交官员的干涉。关于奥古斯丁会代理处的国籍问题，杨先生指出，他已提交证据7和8，以证明奥古斯丁会代理处具有西班牙国籍。他声称，1938年8月12日前西班牙领事的来信证实了这一点，并补充说，即使奥古斯丁会代理处的辩护律师在上次听证会上也承认该机构具有西班牙国籍。他还提及意大利总领事于1938年9月1日写给法院的一封信，信中指出奥古斯丁会代理处作为一个宗教机构，以前属于西班牙。他声称，所有这些均为确凿证据，证明奥古斯丁会代理处过去是、现在仍然是西班牙国籍。

随后他指出，确定法院对某一案件是否有管辖权的时间点是提起诉讼之时。他在此点上引用了《民事诉讼法》第二十七条，并说，在1938年7月23日提起本案诉讼后，法院于8月29日面对奥古斯丁会代理处辩护律师出具的一份证明书。该证明书内容如下：“—致有关各方，兹证明上海奥古斯丁会代理处受意大利管辖，上海，1938年8月26日，意大利代总领事。”

这份证明书之后是意大利总领事于1938年9月1日发出的一封信，他宣读了信中的一段摘录，内容如下：

“我必须提请阁下注意，我对博学法官质疑我的证明书提出抗议，并希望指出，尽管奥古斯丁会代理处作为一个宗教机构以前属于西班牙，但根据我国政府收到的指示，它在中国享有充分的意大利保护，因为本地代理处仅构成奥古斯丁修会的一部分，而其总代理处一直并仍然位于罗马科斯马街（Via dei S. Cosma）48号，因此，法官无权要求详细说明我的法院行使管辖权的细节和理由。”

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS.

SEP 1 O 1938

Consul's Letter
Mr. Yang argued that this letter from the Italian Consul conclusively proved that the Augustinian Procuration was and still was, of Spanish nationality and that there was no change in the status of the mission before or after the filing of the action. Before the filing of the action it was a Spanish mission with offices in Rome, a part of the Augustinian order and after the filing of the action it was still a Spanish mission, a part of the Augustinian order and still with offices in Rome. He, therefore, claimed that the letter from the Italian Consul proved conclusively that the court had jurisdiction over the Augustinian Procuration.
If the Italian Government could claim jurisdiction over a Catholic church merely because it has or maintains an office in Rome, then that Government would have jurisdiction over all British, American, Belgian and French catholic missions scattered all over this country, and the jurisdiction of that Government would extend to 5,000,000 Catholic christians in China and 10,000 Catholic churches in China. He says that the fact that this mission has registered its property with the Italian Government is no reason why this court should lose jurisdiction over this mission. It is common knowledge that many Chinese register their real property through foreign agents in the foreign consulates in Shanghai, but that does not oust the jurisdiction of this court over such Chinese. He also states that the fact that certain members of the Augustinian Procuration have registered themselves with the Italian Consulate is also no legal ground to oust this court of its lawful jurisdiction over this mission. Needless to say there are Chinese, Spanish and other foreign Christians who belong to the Augustinian Procuration—there cannot be such a thing as all the members of that Church registering themselves with the Italian Consulate," Mr. Yang added.

Still Spanish
Dr. G. Sellett, for plaintiffs, then stated that the facts upon which jurisdiction rests were not in dispute. He said that he might accept the statement contained in the letter of the Italian Consulate dated September 1, and if he did so, he came to the question that the court had jurisdiction over the Augustinian Procuration. The Augustinian Procuration which was before the court was a religious organization, organized in Spain, not in Rome or anywhere else, and for many decades has been known in this country as a Spanish religious organization.
The Augustinian Procuration had for many decades been subject to the jurisdiction of the Spanish Consular Court in China and had not been subject to the Italian jurisdiction or Italian Consular Court in China—the facts upon which jurisdiction depended had never been changed and the letter of the Italian Consulate did not indicate the change of a single fact upon which jurisdiction depended. He stated that under the circumstances, he could not see how through a mere decision the Italian Consulate could assume jurisdiction over the Augustinian Procuration.
Judge Li then stated that the court would hear argument on the whole case.

A Protest
Dr. O. Fischer for defendants then said that he protested against the extraordinary procedure of the case. The case was before the court and at the last hearing Mr. Yang asked for an interim ruling regarding the question of jurisdiction. He then stated that he had made no political threats at the last hearing as stated by Dr. Sellett, but merely emphasized that the case was very complicated, involving quite a large sum and he wished the court to exercise great care. He said until the question of jurisdiction was decided, he would request the court not to proceed with the case.
Answering Dr. Fischer's request for an adjournment, Mr. Yang said the question of jurisdiction was brought up not by plaintiff but by the defendants. This question was brought up on August 15 up to date many days had elapsed and counsel for defendant should have prepared everything in the case and should not have asked for further adjournment. The question of jurisdiction was a simple matter.
Judge Li then said he would not render judgment on the question of jurisdiction, but would decide when the whole case had been heard. He adjourned the case to 9.30 a.m. September 16.
Dr. Fischer reserved the right to make further argument on the question of jurisdiction at the next meeting.

领事信函
杨先生辩称，意大利领事的这封信确凿地证明奥古斯丁会代办处（Augustinian Procuration）过去是、现在仍然是西班牙国籍，且在提起诉讼前后，该传教团的地位并未发生任何变化。在提起诉讼之前，它是一个设在罗马设有办事处的西班牙传教团，属于奥古斯丁修会的一部分；在提起诉讼之后，它仍然是一个属于奥古斯丁修会一部分的西班牙传教团，且仍在罗马设有办事处。因此，他声称意大利领事的信确凿地证明了法院对奥古斯丁会代办处拥有管辖权。
如果意大利政府仅仅因为某天主教堂在罗马设有或维持办事处就声称对其拥有管辖权，那么该国政府将对遍布全国的所有英国、美国、比利时和法国天主教传教团拥有管辖权，其管辖范围将涵盖在中国的500万天主教徒和中国的1万座天主教堂。他说，该传教团向意大利政府登记其财产这一事实，并非本庭丧失对该传教团管辖权的理由。众所周知，许多中国人通过外国代理人在上海的外国领事馆登记其不动产，但这并不排除本庭对这些中国人的管辖权。他还指出，奥古斯丁会代办处的某些成员在意大利领事馆登记注册这一事实，也不是排除本庭对该传教团合法管辖权的法律依据。毋庸赘言，属于奥古斯丁会代办处的有中国人、西班牙人和其他外籍基督徒——不可能出现该教会所有成员都在意大利领事馆登记注册的情况，”杨先生补充道。

仍属西班牙籍
原告代理人G. Sellett博士随后表示，作为管辖权依据的事实并无争议。他说，他可以接受意大利领事馆9月1日来函中的陈述，如果接受这一点，那就引出了法院对奥古斯丁会代办处拥有管辖权的问题。提交至法院的奥古斯丁会代办处是一个在西班牙而非罗马或其他地方组织的宗教组织，并且几十年来在中国一直被视为一个西班牙宗教组织。
几十年来，奥古斯丁会代办处一直受西班牙在华领事法庭的管辖，而不受意大利管辖或意大利在华领事法庭的管辖——决定管辖权的事实从未改变，而意大利领事馆的信函并未表明任何决定管辖权的事实发生了改变。他表示，在这种情况下，他看不出意大利领事馆如何能仅凭一项决定就对奥古斯丁会代办处行使管辖权。
李法官随后表示，法院将听取关于整个案件的辩论。

抗议
被告代理人O. Fischer博士随后表示，他抗议本案的非寻常程序。案件已在法院审理中，在上次听证会上，杨先生请求就管辖权问题作出临时裁决。他随后表示，他并未像Sellett博士所说的那样在上次听证会上发出政治威胁，而只是强调案件非常复杂，涉及金额巨大，他希望法院格外谨慎。他说，在管辖权问题得到裁定之前，他将请求法院不要继续审理此案。
针对Fischer博士提出的延期审理请求，杨先生表示，管辖权问题并非由原告而是由被告提出。该问题于8月15日提出，至今已过去多日，被告律师应已准备好案件的一切事宜，不应再要求进一步延期。管辖权问题是一个简单的问题。
李法官随后表示，他不会就管辖权问题作出判决，而是在听取整个案件的审理后再作决定。他将案件延期至9月16日上午9时30分。
Fischer博士保留在下一次开庭时就管辖权问题进一步辩论的权利。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, MAY 23, 1937

Spaniards May Obtain Legal
Protection Of Italians

Persistent Rumours That Italy Will Assume Legal
Jurisdiction Over Citizens Of War-Torn
Nation; Authorities Non-Committal

Persistent rumours that Italy will henceforth assume the position of legal "guardians" of Spaniards residing in Shanghai were received laughingly by Italian Consular authorities.
"Where did you hear that?" demanded Judge R. Rapex, when questioned yesterday. "I have heard nothing about it."
According to reports, however, Italian recognition of the Franco government will be extended to secure the de facto continuation of extraterritorial rights for Spaniards in China, although the Chinese Government has already announced its intention of assuming legal responsibility in the absence of any recognized official of the Spanish Government.
This belief is heightened by the recent case in which a priest, alleged to be a Spaniard, was summoned to the First Special District Court on a charge of slander brought against him by a Russian. In this case the priest claimed that he had acquired Italian citizenship —although not by virtue of the recent alleged agreement. The Chinese court requested the Italian authorities for written confirmation of this fact and the suit is still pending.

Protege Cases Not New
The practice by certain countries of extending privileges for one reason or another is not new to Shanghai, although it has not before been applied except in individual cases or during the early days of the foreigners in China.
The East India Company assumed jurisdiction of every person within their factories and an outgrowth of this practice was the "British protected person," most of them being originally of the Jewish colony in Bombay. In the early days, the American Consul assumed jurisdiction for Swedish citizens and nationals of at least one more country.
Interesting developments as to the status of Spaniards must probably await the time when some charge is brought against a Spanish resident here, and whether or not at that time Italian protection will be afforded to Spaniards without regard to their political sympathies in the present civil war.

然而，据报道，意大利对弗朗哥政府的承认将延伸为确保西班牙人在华治外法权事实上的延续，尽管中国政府已宣布，在没有任何公认的西班牙政府官员的情况下，其打算承担法律责任。
最近发生的一起案件加剧了这种看法：一名据称为西班牙人的神父因一名俄罗斯人对其提起的诽谤指控而被传唤至第一特区法院。在该案中，该神父声称他已获得意大利国籍——尽管并非依据近期所谓的协议。中国法院要求意大利当局对此事实进行书面确认，该诉讼目前仍在 pending（待决/悬而未决）状态。

受保护人案例并非新鲜事
某些国家出于各种原因给予特权的做法在上海并非新鲜事，尽管此前除个别情况或外国人在华早期阶段外，并未应用过这种做法。
东印度公司对其商馆内的每个人行使管辖权，这种做法的产物之一是“英国受保护人”，其中大多数人最初来自孟买的犹太殖民地。在早期，美国领事曾对瑞典公民以及至少另一个国家的国民行使管辖权。
关于西班牙人地位的有趣发展，可能必须等到有针对在此居住的西班牙人的指控提出时才会显现，届时无论其在当前内战中的政治倾向如何，意大利是否都会向西班牙人提供保护，尚待观察。

DEFENDANT FACES
DEFAMATION COUNT

Father Claims To Be
Italian; Accuser Says
He Is Spanish

Mr. Paul Premet, French attorney, yesterday afternoon asked the First Special District Court to issue a warrant for the arrest of Father P. Cerezal, vice-president and Managing Director of the American Securities Corporation, Federal Inc., U.S.A. (Spanish Fathers), for his failure to appear before the tribunal in answer to a summons.

The case concerned is one brought against the father by Joachim Sanchez, former Shanghai importer and exporter, charging defamation of character. Father Cerezal claims Italian nationality and the Italian Consulate-General has confirmed that claim.

In asking for the warrant, Mr. Premet stated that Father Cerezal appears on the books of the United States Department of Commerce as a Spanish citizen, and added that the American office has not yet received any notification of a change in the priest's nationality.

Name Registered

Father Cerezal's name was registered with Department of Commerce several years when the American Securities Corporation was formed. The business of this concern is to handle the financial affairs of what was formerly the Augustinian Procuration.

The case against the priest arose out of remarks he allegedly made against Sanchez's character six or seven years ago in connection with a dispute brought before the First Special District Court concerning a land deal. The name of Sanchez, who had previously left town, was brought into the argument, and Father Cerezal is declared to have assailed him in open court of [illegible] Sanchez re-[illegible] recently and upon hearing of the alleged accusation, commenced to take action. At the time he returned, there was no Spanish Consular Court but shortly after the Chinese tribunal assumed jurisdiction of Spanish nationals in Shanghai, he filed his complaint with that court.

Father Cerezal was issued a summons but he immediately claimed Italian nationality. At a hearing 10 days ago, Sanchez's attorney asked that this claim be investigated and at the conclusion of yesterday's session, they were informed the results of the inquiry.

Date Not Revealed

The court stated that a representative from the tribunal had been sent to the Italian Consulate-General and that he had been informed that the priest was under Italian jurisdiction. The court further stated that the representative asked for the date on which Father Cerezal had changed his nationality but that an answer was not received.

In arguing the matter, Mr. Premet told the court yesterday that according to international law, any tribunal has full power to decide whether or not any defendant summoned before it is subject to its jurisdiction. He added that any court also has the right and duty, in the event a defendant declines jurisdiction, to demand adequate proof of a change of nationality. He further contended that Father Cerezal has not provided adequate proof and that the court is justified in issuing a warrant for his arrest.

The court concluded the hearing by announcing that it was taking a serious view of the case and then remanded the matter sine die.

要求签发逮捕神父的令状

桑切斯寻求地方法院对塞雷萨尔神父发出命令

被告面临诽谤指控

神父声称是意大利人；指控者称他是西班牙人

法国律师保罗·普雷梅特（Paul Premet）先生昨日下午请求第一特区法院签发逮捕令，逮捕美商联邦股份公司（美国西班牙神父会）副总裁兼总经理P. 塞雷萨尔神父，因其未按传票要求出庭应诉。

本案系前上海进出口商乔基姆·桑切斯（Joachim Sanchez）对该神父提起的诉讼，指控其诽谤名誉。塞雷萨尔神父声称拥有意大利国籍，意大利总领事馆已确认了这一说法。

在申请逮捕令时，普雷梅特先生指出，塞雷萨尔神父在美国商务部的登记册上显示为西班牙公民，并补充说，美国方面尚未收到任何关于该神父国籍变更的通知。

名字已注册

塞雷萨尔神父的名字是在几年前美商证券股份公司成立时在商务部注册的。该公司的业务是处理原奥古斯丁修会代理处的财务事务。

针对该神父的案件源于他据称在六七年前的土地交易纠纷中，在第一特区法院审理期间对桑切斯的名誉发表了言论。当时已离沪的桑切斯的名字被卷入争论中，据称塞雷萨尔神父在公开法庭上攻击了[原文不清]桑切斯重新[原文不清]最近，桑切斯在听到这一所谓指控后开始采取行动。在他返回时，尚无西班牙领事法院，但不久之后，中国法庭接管了在上海的西班牙国民的管辖权，他便向该法庭提出了申诉。

法院向塞雷萨尔神父发出了传票，但他立即声称拥有意大利国籍。在十天前的听证会上，桑切斯的律师要求调查这一说法，在昨天的庭审结束时，他们获知了调查结果。

日期未透露

法院表示，已派一名代表前往意大利总领事馆，并被告知该神父受意大利管辖。法院进一步表示，该代表询问了塞雷萨尔神父变更国籍的日期，但未得到答复。

在辩论此事时，普雷梅特先生昨天告诉法院，根据国际法，任何法庭都有完全权力决定被传唤到其面前的任何被告是否受其管辖。他补充说，如果被告拒绝管辖，任何法院也有权利和义务要求提供国籍变更的充分证明。他进一步主张，塞雷萨尔神父未能提供充分证明，法院有理由签发对他的逮捕令。

法院在宣布严肃看待此案后结束了听证会，然后将案件无限期延期。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, APRIL 15, 1937

Two Spanish “Legations” Now
Functioning In Tokyo

TOKYO, April 14.—Spain’s dual government to-day had its exact replica in Tokyo.
Representatives of the Valencia and of the Burgos regimes each held forth in their respective “legations.”
Senor Jose Luis Alvarez, 27-year-old former college instructor in Osaka, who was officially gazetted as Spanish Charge d’Affaires on April 1 and whose letters of appointment were accepted by the Foreign Minister, Mr. Naotake Sato, on April 6, is occupying a single room in the Marunouchi Hotel which he calls “The Legation.”
Senor Juan Gomez de Molina, Counsellor, whose letter of recall was filed with the Foreign Office on April 1, however, still is in possession of the Spanish Legation buildings in Hyoheicho in the exclusive Azabu district.

In addition to Senor de Molina, who had become Chargé d’Affaires since the departure of Senor Santiago Mendez de Vigo, Minister, in August, Senor Francisco del Castillo, former Consul in Kobe, and Senora del Castillo are occupying the official buildings.
Senor De Molina last month made preparations to leave the Legation, but suspended packing operations after reportedly receiving a cablegram from Minister de Vigo, now in Paris.
He has steadfastly refused not only to hand over the buildings and an inventory of the furnishings, but has even declined to see Senor Alvarez, Republican Chargé d’Affaires.
Senor Alvarez has charged Senor De Molina with having destroyed the Republican flag of horizontal red, yellow and purple stripes.—Domei.

瓦伦西亚政权和布尔戈斯政权的代表各自在他们的“公使馆”里发表意见。

Spaniard Falls Down
Steps, Breaks Bone,
Dies, Inquest Finds

Extending its jurisdiction over Spanish nationals who have been temporarily deprived of their extraterritorial rights as an aftermath of the civil war in Spain and the absence of proper diplomatic and consular representation in this country, the First Special District Court this morning conducted an inquest over the body of Rogeliano Mangliog, 68-year-old Spanish watchman born in the Philippine Islands who died at the General Hospital as result of a fatal injury received during a fall.

Employed at the Bell Lumber Company at 117 Thorne Road, Mangliog fell down the stairs at 4.30 p.m. on March 16. He was sent to the General Hospital two days later and it was found that he had broken his rib. He died yesterday morning.

A verdict of death due to accidental injury was returned by Procurator Tang at the Public Mortuary this morning. The body was handed over to the daughter of the deceased.

Ruling Due
By Shihfahpu
On Standing
Of Spaniards

Summonses Here Being
Ignored; Authorities
Seek Instructions

A ruling which will definitely clarify the legal status of Spanish citizens in China is now being considered in Nanking by the Ministry of Justice officials as a result of the failure of several Spaniards to answer summonses of the First Special District Court.

In a recent petition to the Ministry, the local Settlement court officials asked whether Spanish citizens who failed to appear on summons should be arrested according to the customary procedure.

A decision on the question, it was stated, is pending in the next few days.

Spanish nationals in China, as a result of the civil war in their native country, have been without an accredited diplomatic representative. The National Government, through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, announced sometime ago that extraterritorial rights, formerly enjoyed by Spaniards, are now ineffective.

Local courts were notified at the same time that Spanish citizens when they are sued or prosecuted should be dealt with in the same manner as other foreigners who are without consular jurisdiction.

Several summonses, it is understood, have been issued by the Settlement court against local Spaniards for civil suits. In some of these cases, it is reported, the defendants complied with the order of the Court to appear.

据悉，关于此问题的决定将在未来几天内作出。

由于本国发生内战，在华西班牙国民没有 accredited 外交代表。国民政府通过外交部不久前宣布，西班牙人以前享有的治外法权现已失效。

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 4, 1937

Spanish Residents Here
To Be Given No Special
Consideration In Courts

Chinese Government Not Recognizing
Extraterritorial Status Of Nationals;
To Prosecute Cases

Spanish residents residing in Shanghai who are involved in legal proceedings in the special district Chinese courts of the city will be treated in exactly the same way as the nationals of other countries who do not enjoy extraterritorial rights in China. The Chinese Criminal and Civil Codes will be followed to the letter of the law in administering cases in which Spanish citizens are concerned, First Special District Court officials told a CHINA PRESS representative yesterday morning.

Only two or three civil actions against Spanish residents are now pending in the Settlement tribunal but definite action has been taken in these cases as a result of instructions received from Nanking which give the Chinese courts authority to temporarily assume jurisdiction over Spanish nationals.

Being Made Test Case

A test case is being made of a civil action brought against Mr. F. A. Valles, local Spanish resident, by a Greek subject, whose name could not be obtained yesterday by

THE CHINA PRESS. A summons has already been issued but it has not been served. Court employees have made an effort to serve the summons but Mr. Valles has not been available.

It was stated yesterday that a second summons will be issued next week and if employees of the court meet with failure in their efforts to serve that, another will be issued the following week. This third summons will be the last. In accordance with the Chinese Civil Code, a warrant of arrest will then be issued, and the Shanghai Municipal Police will be asked to take the complainant into custody.

The case itself is only a small matter, involving payment of a few hundred dollars. It was first heard in the Spanish Consular Court in 1935 and judgment was handed down in favor of the plaintiff. The judgment was never settled in full, however, and the plaintiff recently revived the case in the Chinese tribunal when the Spanish court ceased to function.

May Try To Settle

At the time the action was presented to the Chinese tribunal, definite instructions regarding the jurisdiction of Spanish nationals had not been received. Now that they have, the way is clear for the courts to proceed.

It was learned yesterday from Spanish sources that an attempt may be made to settle the case out of the court. Whether this will be possible, however, is another matter. It was reported at the court that the tribunal will make it necessary for any settlement, if one is made, to be completed through the regular court channels.

THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MARCH 4, 1937.

JURISDICTION OVER SPANIARDS

THE National Government has finally decided to assume jurisdiction over Spaniards in China. The decision has been reached as the result of the lack of diplomatic or consular representation. Since the withdrawal of Mr. Julio Larracoecha, formerly Acting Spanish Consul-General in Shanghai last autumn, Spaniards have enjoyed no official representation, while at the same time cases involving their compatriots have been accumulating which are liable to affect their own interest as well as that of other nationals.
In order to obviate the difficulty which has thus arisen the National Government has decided to assume jurisdiction over the small number of Spaniards. The intention is a most friendly one. The extension of Chinese jurisdiction will clothe them with certain privileges which may entitle them not only to seek the protection of the territorial Government but also to carry on trade with other nationals. Should their anomalous status be permitted to continue, it is highly probable that no one would care to deal with them for fear of the want of means of legal redress.
The chief question which remains to be answered is whether the Chinese jurisdiction over the Spaniards will be relinquished once the political condition in their homeland is sufficiently stable to permit the maintenance of a competent consular or diplomatic representation in China. To this question no final answer may be given. It would appear correct to suggest that once extrality, is terminated it cannot be re-established without the consent of the territorial Government. Precedents may be found to support this view and it is certain that the National Government of China will not agree to the reinstatement of an antiquated system in this enlightened age. For all practical purposes other nationals dealing with the Spaniards may confidently look forward to legal protection from the Chinese Government and the Spaniards themselves should be happy over the termination of a status which has doubtless caused them not a little embarrassment in this cosmopolitan community.

对西班牙人的管辖权

国民政府最终决定对在华西班牙人行使管辖权。这一决定是由于缺乏外交或领事代表而作出的。自从去年秋天前任代理西班牙驻上海总领事胡里奥·拉拉科埃查（Julio Larracoecha）先生撤离以来，西班牙人一直没有官方代表，与此同时，涉及其同胞的案件不断积累，这可能影响他们自身以及其他国家国民的利益。
为了消除由此产生的困难，国民政府决定对少数西班牙人行使管辖权。这一意图是非常友好的。中国管辖权的延伸将赋予他们某些特权，使他们不仅有权寻求属地政府的保护，还有权与其他国家国民进行贸易。如果允许这种异常状态继续下去，很可能没有人愿意与他们打交道，因为担心缺乏法律补救手段。
仍有待回答的主要问题是，一旦其祖国的政治局势足够稳定，允许在中国维持胜任的领事或外交代表，中国对西班牙人的管辖权是否会放弃。对此问题无法给出最终答案。似乎可以正确地指出，一旦治外法权终止，未经属地政府同意，就不能重新建立。可以找到支持这一观点的先例，而且可以肯定的是，在这个开明的时代，中国国民政府不会同意恢复一种过时的制度。出于所有实际目的，与西班牙人打交道的其他国民可以放心地期待来自中国政府的法律保护，而西班牙人自己也应该为结束这种无疑在这个国际性社区中给他们造成不少尴尬的地位而感到高兴。

CHINA DAILY HERALD, SATURDAY, FEBRUARY 20, 1937

Unprecedented Scandal In
Shanghai

SPANISH EX-CONSUL INVOLVED; MYSTERIOUS
ORDER FOR PASSPORTS

About 130 Spaniards are living now in Shanghai without consular representation and without any official authority to whom they may appeal in time of need and without any superior functionary whatsoever to take official cognizance of their legal capacities in China.

The Spanish community is at the present time a legally impotent and sudderless mass unrepresented by any authority recognized by the national government of China.

Of all the Spanish residents in this city, only one claims to represent Spain in China and his name is Eduardo Vasquez Ferrer.

In statements made over the telephone to a detective of the Shanghai Municipal Police, Mr. Ferrer has declared that he was still issuing Spanish passports. In another statement made over the phone to the same detective Mr. V. Visenzinovich, former chancellor of the

Spanish Consulate, said that Mr. Ferrer was the consul-general appointed by the Spanish Nationalist Government (Franco government).

There is no reason to doubt that Mr. Ferrer was appointed consul-general by the Rebel Government in Spain, but the Chinese government along with most other nations still recognize the Madrid government as the legal government of Spain and thus any person appointed by any other authority than this government has no diplomatic standing in China.

Mr E F. Ferrer was appointed consul-general in Shanghai by the monarchist government in Spain in 1930. Last September, he resigned his post and a notification to that effect was published in the Municipal Gazette for September 11, 1936.

On Mr. Ferrer's resignation, the vice-consul, J. de, Larrecochea, became acting consul and the representative for Spanish residents in this city, but last November Mr. Larrecochea suddenly disappeared from Shanghai, believedly aboard the German vessel Godenfels. On his disappearance Spanish residents ceased to be represented in Shanghai.

Shortly after Larrecochea's departure, Mr. Ferrer is alleged to have transferred all the archives, furniture, seals and other things pertaining to the Spanish government from the former consular offices at 1408 Avenue Joffre to his own possession.

With no consular representation in this city, a curious situation, viewed by some members of the Spanish community with alarm, by others with indifference and by the Consular Body with downright puzzlement, has arisen.

There is no person or official or organ who may order the arrest of a Spanish citizen for some crime committed and as long as China recognizes the extraterritoriality rights of Spanish citizens, any Spaniard may lawfully defy any policeman, coming with any charge or complaint, the right to arrest him.

How long this situation will last remains a matter of concern to the Consular Body and the Spanish community, and depends upon the attitude of the Chinese government.

The whole position of Spanish representation in this country was brought to a head last Wednesday when a Spanish citizen, formerly connected in an official capacity with the Spanish Consulate, complained to police headquarters that Spanish passports were being printed without authority at the Lee Hing Printing Company at 583 Szechuen Road.

In company with a detective of the SMP this citizen called at the shop and found that 50 passports were printed and ready for delivery. On investigation it was found that the printing company was a legal concern and had been printing passports and letterheads for the Spanish Consulate for a number of years. The blocks used in the printing process belonged to the company, having been

made by them from designs tendered some time ago.

Further investigation revealed that 50 passports and 100 letterheads with the Spanish emblem had been ordered by Mr. V. Visenzinovich, former chancellor of the Spanish Consulate. This was confirmed by telephone and Visenzinovich said that he ordered the material to be printed on instructions of the Spanish consul general. When told by police that no such consul at present existed in Shanghai, Visenzinovich answered that the consul was the one appointed by the Spanish Nationalist Government.

To confirm this statement the detective called on Mr. Ferrer at his home at the Cathay Mansions. Mr. Ferrer answered that he is still issuing passports and had ordered the present ones to be printed to be given to persons who wish to go to Spain.

As the proprietors of the printing company did not wish to become entangled in an "international situation" they agreed to let the detective take the passports for the time being. At this point, however, the detective found that his functions as a policeman were not adequate to cover the situation and he went with the Spanish complainant to see Mr. R. T. Bryan, municipal Advocate, S.M.C.

According to statements given to the press by authoritative people, neither of these officials could see any course of action that might possibly be taken without abrogating the extraterritoriality privileges of Spanish citizens in China. There did not and does not exist any Spanish authority to say that Mr. Ferrer had no right to print the passports. If there were to be a complaint, action would have to be taken by the Chinese authorities.

Thus, the matter rested. The passports were returned to the printing company. As they were ordered on the authority of Mr. Ferrer they are his property.

The question has now arisen whether any Spanish citizen may not print passports in Shanghai and dodge arrest for doing so. In the opinion of one Spanish citizen they may do so and further than that may commit any crime without fear of legal arrest.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE 23 FEB 1937）

《字林日报》，1937年2月20日，星期六

上海发生前所未有的丑闻

涉及西班牙前领事；神秘的护照订单

目前约有130名西班牙人居住在上海，没有领事代表，在需要时没有任何官方机构可供求助，也没有任何上级官员正式认可他们在华的法律身份。

西班牙社群目前是一个在法律上无能为力且群龙无首的群体，没有得到中国政府承认的任何当局的代表。

在该市所有西班牙居民中，只有一人声称代表西班牙在华利益，他的名字是爱德华多·巴斯克斯·费雷尔（Eduardo Vasquez Ferrer）。

费雷尔先生在对上海公共租界警务处一名侦探的电话陈述中宣称，他仍在签发西班牙护照。在同一侦探的另一通电话中，西班牙前总领事馆书记员 V. 维森齐诺维奇先生（Mr. V. Visenzinovich）表示，费雷尔先生是由西班牙民族主义政府（佛朗哥政府）任命的总领事。

没有理由怀疑费雷尔先生是由西班牙叛乱政府任命为总领事的，但中国政府以及大多数其他国家仍然承认马德里政府为西班牙的合法政府，因此，由非该政府的其他当局任命的任何人在中国都没有外交地位。

E. F. 费雷尔先生于1930年由西班牙君主制政府任命为驻上海总领事。去年9月，他辞去了职务，相关通知刊登在1936年9月11日的《市政公报》上。

费雷尔先生辞职后，副领事 J. de, Larrecochea（音译：拉雷科切亚）成为代理领事及本市西班牙居民的代表，但去年11月，拉雷科切亚先生突然从上海消失，据信是登上了德国船只“戈登费尔斯号”（Godenfels）。随着他的消失，西班牙居民在上海不再有人代表。

据称，在拉雷科切亚离开后不久，费雷尔先生将原位于霞飞路1408号的前领事馆办公室内属于西班牙政府的所有档案、家具、印章及其他物品转移至其个人占有之下。

由于本市没有领事代表，出现了一种奇特的局面，西班牙社群中的一些成员对此感到恐慌，另一些人则漠不关心，而领事团则感到彻底困惑。

没有任何人、官员或机构可以下令逮捕犯有某种罪行的西班牙公民，只要中国承认西班牙公民的治外法权，任何西班牙人都可以合法地蔑视任何带着指控或投诉前来逮捕他的警察。

这种情况将持续多久，仍是领事团和西班牙社群关注的问题，这取决于中国政府的态度。

上周三，西班牙在华代表地位问题达到了顶点，当时一名曾在西班牙领事馆担任官方职务的西班牙公民向警察总局投诉，称四川路583号的李兴印刷公司（Lee Hing Printing Company）正在未经授权印制西班牙护照。

这名公民在上海公共租界警务处一名侦探的陪同下前往该店，发现已有50本护照印制完毕，准备交付。经调查，该印刷公司是合法企业，多年来一直为西班牙领事馆印制护照和信头。印刷过程中使用的印版归该公司所有，是他们根据不久前提供的设计制作的。

进一步调查显示，50本护照和100张带有西班牙徽章的信头是由西班牙前总领事馆书记员 V. 维森齐诺维奇先生订购的。这一点通过电话得到了确认，维森齐诺维奇表示，他是按照西班牙总领事的指示订购这些材料的。当警方告诉他上海目前没有这样的领事时，维森齐诺维奇回答说，该领事是由西班牙民族主义政府任命的。

为了证实这一说法，侦探前往费雷尔先生位于国泰公寓（Cathay Mansions）的住所拜访。费雷尔先生回答称，他仍在签发护照，并已下令印制目前的护照，提供给希望前往西班牙的人。

由于印刷公司的业主不希望卷入“国际局势”，他们同意让侦探暂时拿走这些护照。然而，此时侦探发现，他作为警察的职权不足以应对这种情况，于是他与这位西班牙投诉人一起去见上海公共租界工部局市政检察官 R. T. 布莱恩先生（Mr. R. T. Bryan）。

据权威人士向媒体发表的声明，这两位官员都看不出在不废除西班牙公民在华治外法权特权的情况下可能采取的任何行动方针。过去和现在都不存在任何西班牙当局来认定费雷尔先生无权印制护照。如果要提出投诉，必须由中国当局采取行动。

因此，此事就此搁置。护照被退还给印刷公司。由于它们是依据费雷尔先生的授权订购的，因此属于他的财产。

现在出现的问题是，是否任何西班牙公民都可以在上海印制护照并借此逃避逮捕。据一位西班牙公民认为，他们可以这样做，甚至更进一步，可以实施任何罪行而不必担心被合法逮捕。

（印章：上海公共租界工部局警务处 1937年2月23日）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, February 20, 1937

Spanish Consul Denounced

Ferrer Lacking
Authority Here,
Says Ex-Attache

Spaniards Of Shanghai
Unrepresented; New
Statement Issued

U.S. CONSULATE
DODGES PASSPORT

Government Of Burgos
Not Recognized
By China

Promising that Spanish residents of Shanghai will soon have a legal representative here and openly denouncing Mr. Eduardo Vasquez Ferrer as a "bogus" consul and defying him to take jurisdiction over Spanish citizens in Shanghai, Mr. I. J. Sanchez, commercial attache of the Spanish Consulate in Shanghai in 1930 and 1931, this morning issued a statement to the press denying that Ferrer had the authority to levy a fine or give a decision in a traffic case, as Ferrer was reported to have said he had.

In line with a story printed in this newspaper yesterday, Sanchez claims that no law or law authority exists in the Spanish community at present and completely refutes Mr. Ferrer's statements that this condition is imaginary.

"Bogus Consul"

The signed statement of Mr. Sanchez follows:

"The question of court jurisdiction is one to be decided by the Chinese government and Spain.

As stated in a letter to Sir John Brenan, Ferrer is a bogus consul and I defy him to issue a warrant for my arrest if he thinks I am rebelling against the authority of his court.

"I do not wish to commit an offence intentionally but, as a motorcar driver it is possible for me to inadvertently break any of the traffic regulations and in this case I defy the S.M.P. to report the matter to Ferrer and defy him (Ferrer) to impose a fine upon me. He refers in his statement reported in a morning newspaper that on January 21 the U.M.P. traffic department referred a case against a Spaniard to him. For their effect I will send a letter of complaint to the secretary of the Shanghai Municipal Council to stop this illegal procedure.

"Committed Crime"

"That no law or law authorities exist at present is not imaginary. Ferrer has committed a crime ordering the printing of the passports and the S.M.P. with all the facts in their hands can not arrest him and can not seize the printed matter without the order of a competent authority.

"Ferrer should know that any passport issued by him is useless and that local authorities will not recognize them.

"In due course and sooner than expected Spain will have here in Shanghai its legal representative and then all these irregular activities of Ferrer will be stopped."

Signed Passport

In connection with the statement about passports it is known that Ferrer signed his name as consul for the Burgos government on the passport of the young son of Mrs. Linda Cohen recently and that this passport was brought before the American authorities to be visaed.

It so happened that the passport was issued sometime ago by Ferrer when he was consul-general for Spain in Shanghai; the passport has about three months to run before it expires. Wishing to avoid difficulties, Cohen went to Ferrer to have the passport renewed and Ferrer renewed it in his "capacity" as consul for the Burgos government.

Ignored Renewal

As the United States does not recognise the Burgos government as the national government of Spain, local American officials were of course unable to recognise the renewal made by Ferrer and have chosen to ignore the renewal but to honor the old passport which has not yet expired. As Cohen intends to enter the United States as an immigrant, the question of renewing this passport will not arise.

In cases where Spanish passports have already expired it is believed that no governments, with the possible exception of Germany and Italy, would recognise passports issued by representatives of the Burgos government.

Status Unaffected

While Mr. Ferrer claims that he is still recognised by the majority of Spanish citizens in Shanghai as the representative of their country and while this statement may be true, it does not affect his status one iota, it is pointed out. The government of China is the only body that can recognise Mr. Ferrer as consul for Spain and as far the Nanking government has not recognised the Burgos government and hence does not recognise Mr. Ferrer who claims to represent that government.

Commenting on Mr. Ferrer's statements as reported in a morning newspaper today to the effect that he is still exercising his authority as a consular judge, handling police cases and levying fines when necessary, several consular officials and Spanish citizens this morning admitted that Mr. Ferrer simply and plainly has no authority to do so.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年2月20日，星期六

西班牙领事遭谴责

前随员称费雷尔
在此无权

在沪西班牙人
无人代表；发布
新声明

美国领事馆
回避护照问题

布尔戈斯政府
未获中国承认

曾于1930年和1931年担任西班牙驻上海领事馆商务随员的I. J. 桑切斯（I. J. Sanchez）先生今晨向报界发表声明，否认爱德华多·巴斯克斯·费雷尔（Eduardo Vasquez Ferrer）先生拥有征收罚款或对交通案件作出裁决的权力——据称费雷尔曾声称自己拥有此类权力。桑切斯承诺在沪西班牙居民很快将在此拥有合法代表，并公开谴责费雷尔为“假冒”领事，挑战其对在沪西班牙公民行使管辖权。

鉴于本报昨日刊登的一则报道，桑切斯声称目前西班牙社群中不存在任何法律或法律权威，并完全驳斥了费雷尔关于这种状况是虚构的说法。

“假冒领事”

桑切斯先生的署名声明如下：

“法院管辖权的问题应由中华民国政府和西班牙决定。

正如我在致约翰·布伦南爵士（Sir John Brenan）的信中所陈述，费雷尔是一名假冒领事，如果他认为我是在反抗其法院的权威，我挑战他签发对我的逮捕令。

“我无意故意犯罪，但作为一名汽车驾驶员，我可能会无意中违反任何交通规则，在这种情况下，我挑战上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）将此案报告给费雷尔，并挑战他（费雷尔）对我处以罚款。他在一家晨报报道的声明中提到，1月21日，工部局警务处交通科将一起针对一名西班牙人的案件移交给了他。为了产生效力，我将向上海工部局秘书发送一封投诉信，以制止这种非法程序。

“犯下罪行”

“目前不存在法律或法律权威并非虚构。费雷尔下令印制护照已构成犯罪，而掌握全部事实的工部局警务处在没有主管当局命令的情况下，无法逮捕他，也无法扣押印刷品。

“费雷尔应该知道，由他签发的任何护照都是无效的，地方当局不会予以承认。

“在适当的时候，而且比预期的要早，西班牙将在上海设立其合法代表，届时费雷尔的所有这些违规活动都将停止。”

签署护照

关于护照的声明，据悉费雷尔最近在琳达·科恩（Linda Cohen）女士幼子的护照上以布尔戈斯政府领事的身份签署了姓名，该护照随后被提交给美国当局申请签证。

碰巧的是，该护照是费雷尔此前担任西班牙驻上海总领事时签发的；该护照距到期还有约三个月时间。科恩女士为避免麻烦，去找费雷尔更新护照，费雷尔便以他作为布尔戈斯政府领事的“身份”更新了护照。

无视更新

由于美国不承认布尔戈斯政府为西班牙的国家政府，当地美国官员自然无法承认费雷尔所作的更新，并选择忽略该更新，而是认可尚未过期的旧护照。由于科恩打算以移民身份进入美国，因此不会出现更新此护照的问题。

在西班牙护照已经过期的情况下，据信除德国和意大利外，没有任何政府会承认由布尔戈斯政府代表签发的护照。

地位不受影响

有人指出，虽然费雷尔先生声称他仍被上海大多数西班牙公民承认为其国家的代表，且这一说法可能是真的，但这丝毫不会影响他的地位。只有中国政府有权承认费雷尔先生为西班牙领事，而南京国民政府尚未承认布尔戈斯政府，因此也不承认声称代表该政府的费雷尔先生。

针对今晨一家晨报报道的费雷尔先生的言论——即他仍在行使作为领事法官的权力，处理警察案件并在必要时征收罚款——几位领事官员和西班牙公民今晨承认，费雷尔先生显然无权这样做。

While officially no Spanish consular service exists in Shanghai or any other cities in China, complaints against local Spaniards are still being filed by the Shanghai Municipal Police with Mr. Eduardo Vasquez Ferrer who resigned his post as representative of the Republican Spanish Government on August 3., 1936.
Mr. Ferrer, who says that he has since been resumed to his post by the Spanish Nationalist Government (Franco Government), revealed to THE CHINA PRESS last night that he is still exercising his authority as a consular judge, handling police cases and levying fines when necessary.
To all intent and purposes, he said, he still represents the Spanish community in Shanghai and is exercising Spain's extraterritorial rights in consular jurisdiction, although the Government which named him to his post has not been recognized by the National Government of China.
Denies Factionalism Here
The aged Spanish official, who had been Spanish Consul-General since 1899, denied yesterday that as a result of the war in Spain, the Spanish community of 130 people here is torn by strife, devoid of legal rights and thrown into a situation whereby no law or law authority exists.
To prove that he is still recognised by the Shanghai Municipal Police as a Spanish Consul-General Shanghai, Mr. Ferrer showed a CHINA PRESS reporter a copy of a traffic complaint filed by the S.M.P. on January 22. This was against a Spanish citizen and Mr. Ferrer, despite his unofficial capacity, says he has the authority to levy fine or give any other kind of decision in the case.
The version that no law or law authority exists at present in the local Spanish community, Mr. Ferrer said, "is more or less imaginary. 'The Spanish people here as a whole, except for an insignificant minority, recognize me as their Consul and my authority attached thereto,' he said.
From official foreign consular sources, it was further learned yesterday, that despite the general impression otherwise, Spanish citizens here are still subject to arrest, in the event that they happen to commit crimes.
In regard to civil actions, steps are now being taken, as a result of the pending official non-existence of Spanish consular officials, to determine the procedure in handling such cases.
About three weeks ago, an action was brought in the First Special District Court on Courtenay Road, the British Consulate, against a Spanish citizen, in view of the fact that the Spanish government represented by China enjoys extraterritorial privileges, the case was rejected, it was stated, and referred to the S.M.C. Another was brought to attention of the Consular Body, it was said, and it was recommended the case be placed before him for disposal.
Not Up To Consular Body
The question of jurisdiction over Spanish nationals living in Shanghai or elsewhere in China is not a matter for the Consular Body, members of that group told THE CHINA PRESS last night. But rather an issue between Spain and the Foreign Ministry. Since there is no Spanish consular service in Shanghai, it was stated, the Foreign Ministry at Nanking is in a position to take the initiative and set machinery in motion implementing extraterritorial rights, thereby bringing the Spanish citizens in the country under the jurisdiction of the Chinese courts.
In the event that a Spanish citizen should commit a crime of a major nature, the matter of jurisdiction would be referred to the Foreign Ministry at Nanking. The man, however, would not be permitted to remain at large by the local police, THE CHINA PRESS was told. Rather, as an enemy of society and a criminal, he would be arrested and detained pending a settlement of the jurisdiction issue, after which he would be handed over to the authorities empowered to act against him.
The present policy, the nature of which has not been revealed, but which is believed to be dual, is expected to provide the necessary test case for settlement of the issue, at least on a temporary basis.
Question Of Passports
The question of jurisdiction of Spanish citizens residing in Shanghai arose yesterday, when it was revealed that Mr. Ferrer, stricken that some Spanish passports he printed.
The order for the passports was given to the Lee Hing Printing Company by Mr. V. Vlassinevich, former chanceller of the Spanish Consulate-General under Mr. Ferrer. Vlassinevich told the police that instructions to do so were given him by Mr. Ferrer.
Mr. Ferrer told the reporter that he is issuing passports to Spanish citizens who need them.
The investigation into the ordering of the passports was made on a complaint taken to the police by a Spanish resident of Shanghai named Santian. The police found that such an order had been issued. He is said to have informed the police that he had placed the order and explained that he issued instructions for the printing of the
passports because of his appointment by the Nationalist Government.
The complaint against Mr. Ferrer and his printing of passports has prompted a letter to Sir John Mason, British Consul-General and senior consul, protesting. He asserts that Mr. Ferrer's taking over of the archives of the Spanish Consulate-General last year was unlawful and asks for action. He refers to the present situation in Shanghai as regards Spanish residents as "anomalous." He adds that unless the Consular Body takes steps to take the archives away from Mr. Ferrer, he will present the case to the Foreign Ministry at Nanking.
THE CHINA PRESS was informed by Consular Body members last night that it was unlikely that the Body would act since the affair was not its concern.
Mr. Ferrer took the archives of the consulate-general last year after the disappearance of Mr. J. de Larracoechea, who became acting consul for the Loyalist Government after Mr. Ferrer's resignation, and then left town.

费雷尔称
他仍在此
行使领事职权
否认西班牙社群
存在纷争；护照
问题成为焦点

虽然在上海或中国其他城市官方上已不存在西班牙领事服务，但上海公共租界工部局警务处仍在向爱德华多·巴斯克斯·费雷尔先生提交针对当地西班牙人的投诉。费雷尔曾于1936年8月3日辞去西班牙共和政府代表的职务。

费雷尔先生称，此后他已被西班牙国民政府（佛朗哥政府）恢复职务，他昨晚向《字林西报》透露，他仍在行使作为领事法官的权力，处理警察案件并在必要时征收罚款。

他说，就所有意图和目的而言，他仍然代表上海的西班牙社群，并在领事管辖权方面行使西班牙的治外法权，尽管任命他任职的政府尚未获得中国国民政府的承认。

否认本地派系斗争

这位自1899年起担任西班牙总领事的年迈西班牙官员昨天否认，由于西班牙战争，这里130人的西班牙社群陷入纷争、缺乏法律权利并陷入无法无天的境地。

为了证明他仍被上海公共租界工部局警务处承认为西班牙驻上海总领事，费雷尔先生向《字林西报》记者展示了一份工部局警务处于1月22日提交的交通投诉副本。该投诉针对一名西班牙公民，费雷尔先生表示，尽管他处于非官方身份，但他有权对此案处以罚款或作出任何其他类型的裁决。

费雷尔先生说，关于当地西班牙社群目前不存在法律或法律权威的说法，“多少有些虚构”。他说：“这里的西班牙人整体而言，除了微不足道的少数派外，都承认我是他们的领事以及随之而来的权威。”

昨日从外国领事界的官方消息来源进一步获悉，尽管普遍印象并非如此，但这里的西班牙公民如果犯罪，仍然会被逮捕。

关于民事诉讼，由于西班牙领事官员在官方上暂缺，目前正在采取措施以确定处理此类案件的程序。

大约三周前，在英国领事馆位于库尔特尼路（Courtenay Road）的第一特区法院对一名西班牙公民提起诉讼，鉴于中国所代表的西班牙政府享有治外法权特权，据说该案被驳回并转交上海工部局（S.M.C.）。据说另一起案件引起了领事团的注意，并建议将该案提交给他处理。

不属于领事团职权范围

领事团成员昨晚告诉《字林西报》，居住在 Shanghai 或中国其他地方的西班牙国民的管辖权问题不是领事团的事务，而是西班牙与外交部之间的问题。据说，由于上海没有西班牙领事服务，南京外交部有能力采取主动并启动机制实施治外法权，从而将在华西班牙公民置于中国法院的管辖之下。

如果西班牙公民犯下重大罪行，管辖权问题将提交南京外交部处理。然而，《字林西报》获悉，当地警方不会允许此人逍遥法外。相反，作为社会公敌和罪犯，他将被逮捕并拘留，等待管辖权问题解决，之后他将移交给有权对他采取行动的当局。

目前的政策性质尚未披露，但据信具有双重性，预计至少会在临时基础上为解决该问题提供必要的测试案例。

护照问题

昨天，当揭露费雷尔先生下令印制了一些西班牙护照时，居住在上海的西班牙公民的管辖权问题浮出水面。

印制护照的命令是由前西班牙总领事馆随员V. 弗拉西涅维奇（V. Vlassinevich）先生下达给李兴印刷公司（Lee Hing Printing Company）的。弗拉西涅维奇告诉警方，是费雷尔先生指示他这样做的。

费雷尔先生告诉记者，他正在向需要护照的西班牙公民签发护照。

对订购护照的调查源于一位名为桑蒂安（Santian）的上海西班牙居民向警方提出的投诉。警方发现确实发出了此类订单。据说他告知警方是他下的订单，并解释说他指示印制护照是因为他得到了国民政府的任命。

针对费雷尔先生及其印制护照行为的投诉促使人们致信英国总领事兼首席领事约翰·梅森爵士（Sir John Mason），提出抗议。他断言费雷尔先生去年接管西班牙总领事馆档案的行为是非法的，并要求采取行动。他将目前上海西班牙居民的处境称为“反常”。他补充说，除非领事团采取措施从费雷尔先生手中夺回档案，否则他将把此案提交南京外交部。

《字林西报》昨晚从领事团成员处获悉，领事团不太可能采取行动，因为此事与其无关。

去年，在J. 德·拉拉科切亚（J. de Larracoechea）先生失踪后，费雷尔先生接管了总领事馆的档案。拉拉科切亚先生在费雷尔辞职后成为效忠派政府的代理领事，随后离开了本市。

DC (G)

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, February 19, 1937

Spain And
Extraterritoriality
(An Editorial)

SPAIN'S EMERGENCY has developed a sensational "China angle" which in our opinion vitally affects the other extraterritorial nations.

Disclosure of the fact that Spain now competely lacks recognised consular representation in Shanghai creates most dangerous potentialities.

It is our belief that the extraterritorial nations and Spanish residents in Shanghai, whatever Spanish political belief, should move without delay to bring about a situation of recognised consular representation—for if they do not, China cannot be blamed for taking matters into her own hands in fashion distressing to the Spaniards, and bound to be regarded by other extraterritorial Powers as setting a most undesirable precedent.

As matters stand, the Spanish Consul has resigned and the Spanish Acting Consul-General has disappeared, leaving in Shanghai only the former Spanish Consul who has set up shop in the role of Consul for a revolutionary Government not recognized by China.

This situation came to light as result of the activities of this gentleman in printing off passports said to be for issuance to persons who might desire thus automatically to become citizens of Spain. Not mentioned but obviously a possibility is the fact that White Russian ex-officers, desperate here and anxious to fight either for or against a revolution anywhere, might be glad to become Spanish citizens thus easily and take up arms for a Spanish White movement. That the former Consul has no more legal right either to print passports or to issue them to non-Spaniards is, however, a problem rather for the Spanish themselves to settle than for others to view with more than interest and curiosity. The extraterritoriality issue is fundamental, and affects others vitally.

Perhaps it may be argued that merely because a nation has extraterritoriality, that is no reason why it should concern itself with the existence of a scandalous situation of another extraterritorial nation. The point is this: since Spain at present lacks any means of administering her own laws against Spanish citizens here, there is the most excellent of opportunities for China to say that Spanish extraterritoriality has virtually abolished itself and that Chinese law and courts will henceforth apply to Spaniards in China.

Which, we submit, is an extremely poor method of progressive abolition of extraterritoriality. It has dangerous potentialities for all extraterritorial Powers, obviously; the abolition of extraterritoriality should be a question not of the temporary embarrassment of some extraterritorial nation, but of universal agreement that the Chinese judiciary has developed to a point where retention of extraterritoriality is not necessary.

We all know that the Spanish Government has more than enough troubles. But the appointment of a regularly recognised Consul here need be little more than a formality. We are certain that there must be qualified men here ready and anxious to serve as an honorary matter if necessary. The Spanish community is generally law-abiding and there should be no backbreaking assortment of duties for a Consul. But in any event, as a matter of urgent necessity the present situation should not be allowed to progress further.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1937年2月19日，星期五

西班牙与
治外法权
（社论）

西班牙的紧急事态发展出了一个耸人听闻的“中国角度”，在我们看来，这严重影响到其他享有治外法权的国家。

披露西班牙目前在上海完全缺乏被承认的领事代表这一事实，造成了最危险的潜在可能性。

我们相信，享有治外法权的各国以及在上海的西班牙居民，无论其持有何种西班牙政治信仰，都应立即采取行动，促成被承认的领事代表局面的出现——因为如果他们不这样做，就不能责怪中国以令西班牙人苦恼的方式自行处理事务，而这必然会被其他享有治外法权的列强视为树立了一个极不可取的先例。

就现状而言，西班牙领事已辞职，西班牙代理总领事已失踪，留在上海的只有前西班牙领事，他以一个未被中国承认的革命政府领事的身份开设了办事机构。

这一情况是因这位先生活动而曝光的，他印制据称是发给那些希望以此自动成为西班牙公民的人的护照。虽未提及但显然存在的一种可能性是，在此地走投无路、急于在任何地方为革命一方或反革命一方作战的沙俄白军前军官，可能会乐于如此轻易地成为西班牙公民，并为西班牙的白色运动拿起武器。然而，前领事既无权印制护照，也无权向非西班牙人签发护照，这个问题与其说是让他人带着多于兴趣和好奇的态度去看待的问题，不如说是应由西班牙人自己解决的问题。治外法权问题是根本性的，并严重影响着其他国家。

或许有人争辩说，仅仅因为一个国家拥有治外法权，并没有理由让它去关心另一个享有治外法权国家存在的丑闻局面。要点在于：由于西班牙目前缺乏任何手段对其在沪公民执行本国法律，这就为中国提供了绝好的机会，声称西班牙的治外法权实际上已自行废除，此后中国法律和法院将适用于在华西班牙人。

我们认为，这是一种极其糟糕的逐步废除治外法权的方法。显然，这对所有享有治外法权的列强都具有危险的潜在影响；废除治外法权不应取决于某个享有治外法权国家的暂时困境，而应基于普遍共识，即中国司法体系已发展到不再需要保留治外法权的程度。

我们都知道西班牙政府麻烦缠身。但在此任命一位获得正式承认的领事只需走个过场。我们确信，这里一定有合格的人士愿意并在必要时以荣誉性质任职。西班牙侨民群体通常守法，领事不应面临繁重的职责负担。但无论如何，出于迫切的必要，不应允许目前的局势进一步恶化。

Legal Silence Binds 130 Shanghai Iberians
Without Consular Representation; Passports
Issued By Former Madrid Consul Questioned

Consular Body Facing
Delicate Task; Police
Said Without Power

Ferrer, Resigned Representative Of Regime
Recognized By China, Claims To Function
With All Governmental Prerogatives

COURT OF CONSULS INVOLVED

By JACK BELDEN

SOME 130 Spaniards are today living in Shanghai
without consular representation without fear of
arrest, without any official authority to whom they may
appeal in time of need and without any superior func-
tionary whatsoever to take official cognizance of their
legal capacities in China.

The Spanish community is at the present time a
legally incoherent and rudderless mass unrepresented by
any authority recognized by the national government of
China.

FERRER CLAIMS POST

Of all the Spanish residents in this city, only one claims
to represent Spain in China and his name is Eduardo Vas-
quez Ferrer, consul-general for Spain from 1930 until Septem-
ber of last year, when he resigned his post.

In statements made over the telephone to a detective
of the Shanghai Municipal Police, Mr. Ferrer has declared
that he was still issuing
Spanish passports. In an-
other statement made over
the phone to the same detec-
tive, Mr. V. Visentinovich,
former chancellor of the
Spanish Consulate, said that
Mr. Ferrer was the consul-
general appointed by the
Spanish Nationalist Govern-
ment (Franco government).

Madrid Still Recognized

There is no reason to doubt
that Mr. Ferrer was appoint-
ed consul-general by the
Rebel Government in Spain,
but the Chinese government
along with most other
nations still recognizes the Madrid
government as the legal govern-
ment of Spain and thus any per-
son appointed by any other
authority than this government
has no diplomatic standing in
China.

Mr. E. F. Ferrer was appointed
consul-general in Shanghai by the
monarchist government in Spain
in 1930. Last September, he re-
signed his post and a notification
to that effect was published
in the Municipal Gazette for
September 11, 1938.

Vice Consul Disappears

On Mr. Ferrer's resignation, the
vice-consul, J. de Larracoechea,
became acting consul and
the representative for Spanish
residents in this city. But
late November Mr. Larracoechea
suddenly disappeared from Shang-
hai, believedly aboard the German
vessel Gneisenau. On his dis-
appearance, Spanish residents
ceased to be represented in
Shanghai.

Shortly after Larracoechea's de-
parture, Mr. Ferrer is alleged to
have transferred all the archives,
furniture, seals and other things
pertaining to the Spanish govern-
ment from the former consular
offices at 1409 Avenue Joffre to his
own possession.

Case Pending

With no consular representa-
tion in this city, a curious situa-
tion, viewed by some members of
the Spanish community with
alarm, by others with indifference
and by the Consular Body with
downright puzzlement, has arisen.

There is no person or official or
organ who may order the arrest
of a Spanish citizen for some
crime committed and as long as
China recognizes the extraterri-
toriality rights of Spanish
citizens, any Spaniard may lawfully
deny any policeman, coming
with any charge or complaint, the
right to arrest him.

Depends On Nanking

How long this situation will last
remains a matter of concern to
the Consular Body and the
Spanish community, and depends
upon the attitude of the Chinese
government.

The whole position of Spanish
representation in this country was
brought to a head last Wednesday
when a Spanish citizen, formerly
connected in an official capacity
with the Spanish Consulate, com-
plained to police headquarters
that Spanish passports were being
printed without authority at the
Lee Sing Printing Company at
688 Szechuen Road.

Passports Found

In company with a detective
of the SMP this citizen called
at the shop and found that
50 passports were printed and
ready for delivery. On in-
vestigation it was found that the
printing company was a legal
concern and had been printing
passports and letterheads for the
Spanish Consulate for a number
of years. The blocks used in the
printing process belonged to the
company, having been made by
them from designs tendered some
time ago.

Further investigation revealed
that 50 passports and 100 letter-
heads with the Spanish emblem
had been ordered by Mr. V.
Visentinovich, former chancellor
of the Spanish Consulate. This
was confirmed by telephone and
Visentinovich said that he order-
ed the material to be printed on
instructions of the Spanish con-
sul-general. When told by police
that no such consul at present
existed in Shanghai, Visentinovich
answered that the consul was the
one appointed by the Spanish
Nationalist Government.

Admits Issuing Passports

To confirm this statement, the
detective called Mr. Ferrer at his
home at the Cathay Mansions.
Mr. Ferrer answered that he is
still issuing passports and had
ordered the present ones to be
printed to be given to persons who
wish to go to Spain.

Detectives Stumped

As the proprietors of the print-
ing company did not wish to be-
come entangled in an "interna-
tional situation" they agreed to
let the detective take the passports
for the time being. At this point,
however, the detective found that
his functions as a policeman were
not adequate to cover the situation
and he went with the Spanish
complainant to see Mr. R. T.
Bryan, municipal Advocate, S.M.C.

During the interview with Mr.
Bryan, it so chanced that Mr. E.
A. Long, secretary of the Consular
Body, was present. According to
statements given to a representa-
tive of the Shanghai Evening
Post, by other persons present at
the conference, neither of these of-
ficials could see any course of ac-
tion that might possibly be taken
without abrogating the extraterri-
toriality privileges of Spanish
citizens in China. There did not
and does not exist any Spanish
authority to say that Mr. Ferrer
had no right to print the pass-
ports. If there were to be a com-
plaint, action would have to be
taken by the Chinese authorities.

Passports Returned

There, the matter rested. The
passports were returned to the
printing company. As they were
ordered on the authority of Mr.
Ferrer they are his property.

The question has now arisen
whether any Spanish citizen may
not print passports in Shanghai
and dodge arrest for doing so. In
the opinion of one Spanish citizen
they may do so and further than
that may commit any crime
without fear of legal arrest.

缺乏领事代表使130名在上海的伊比利亚人
受制于法律真空；前马德里领事签发的
护照受到质疑

领事团面临
微妙任务；警方
据说无权行事

费雷尔，已被中国承认政权辞职的代表，
声称行使所有政府特权

涉及领事法庭

作者：杰克·贝尔登 (Jack Belden)

目前约有130名西班牙人生活在上海，没有领事代表，不担心被捕，在需要时没有任何官方权威机构可供申诉，也没有任何上级官员正式认可他们在中国的法律地位。

西班牙侨民群体目前在法律上是一个连贯性缺失、群龙无首的群体，没有得到中国政府承认的任何当局的代表。

费雷尔声称拥有职位

在本市所有西班牙居民中，只有一人声称代表西班牙在华利益，他的名字是爱德华多·巴斯克斯·费雷尔 (Eduardo Vasquez Ferrer)，他从1930年起担任西班牙总领事，直到去年9月辞职。

费雷尔先生在对上海公共租界工部局警务处一名侦探的电话陈述中宣称，他仍在签发
西班牙护照。在同一位侦探的另一次电话陈述中，西班牙领事馆前书记官 V. 维森蒂诺维奇 (V. Visentinovich) 先生说，费雷尔先生是由西班牙国民政府（佛朗哥政府）任命的总领事。

马德里仍获承认

没有理由怀疑费雷尔先生是由西班牙叛乱政府任命为总领事的，但中国政府以及大多数其他国家仍然承认马德里政府为西班牙的合法政府，因此由该政府以外的任何当局任命的任何人在中国都没有外交地位。

E. F. 费雷尔先生于1930年由西班牙君主制政府任命为上海总领事。去年9月，他辞去职务，相关通知刊登在1938年9月11日的《市政公报》上。

副领事失踪

费雷尔先生辞职后，副领事 J. 德·拉腊科切亚 (J. de Larracoechea) 成为代理领事和本市西班牙居民的代表。但在11月下旬，拉腊科切亚先生突然从上海消失，据信是登上了德国船只“格奈森瑙”号 (Gneisenau)。随着他的消失，西班牙居民在上海不再有代表。

据称，在拉腊科切亚离开后不久，费雷尔先生将所有属于西班牙政府的档案、家具、印章和其他物品从位于霞飞路1409号的前领事馆办公室转移到了他自己手中。

案件悬而未决

由于本市没有领事代表，出现了一种奇特的局面，西班牙侨民群体中的一些人对此感到惊慌，另一些人则漠不关心，而领事团则感到彻底困惑。

没有任何人、官员或机构可以下令逮捕犯有某种罪行的西班牙公民，只要中国承认西班牙公民的治外法权权利，任何西班牙人都可以合法地拒绝任何带着指控或投诉前来的警察逮捕他的权利。

取决于南京

这种状况会持续多久，仍是领事团和西班牙侨民群体关注的问题，并取决于中国政府的态度。

上周三，当一名曾在西班牙领事馆担任官方职务的西班牙公民向警察总局投诉，称在四川路688号的李生印刷公司 (Lee Sing Printing Company) 正在未经授权印制西班牙护照时，西班牙在华代表权的整个问题达到了顶点。

发现护照

这位公民在一名工部局警务处侦探的陪同下前往该店，发现已印制好50本护照，准备交付。经调查，该印刷公司是合法企业，多年来一直为西班牙领事馆印制护照和信头。印刷过程中使用的印版归该公司所有，是他们根据不久前提供的设计制作的。

进一步调查显示，50本护照和100张带有西班牙徽章的信头是由西班牙领事馆前书记官 V. 维森蒂诺维奇先生订购的。这一点通过电话得到证实，维森蒂诺维奇表示，他是按照西班牙总领事的指示订购这些材料的。当警方告知他上海目前没有这样的领事时，维森蒂诺维奇回答说，该领事是由西班牙国民政府任命的。

承认签发护照

为了证实这一说法，侦探打电话到费雷尔先生位于华懋公寓 (Cathay Mansions) 的家中。费雷尔先生回答说，他仍在签发护照，并已下令印制目前的护照，发给希望前往西班牙的人。

侦探陷入困境

由于印刷公司的业主不愿卷入“国际局势”，他们同意让侦探暂时拿走护照。然而，此时侦探发现，他作为警察的职能不足以应对这一局面，于是他与西班牙投诉人一起去见工部局市政检察官 R. T. 布莱恩 (R. T. Bryan) 先生。

在与布莱恩先生面谈期间，碰巧领事团秘书 E. A. 朗 (E. A. Long) 先生也在场。根据出席会议的其他人士向《上海晚邮报》代表提供的陈述，这两位官员都看不出在不废除西班牙公民在华治外法权特权的情况下可能采取的任何行动方案。当时不存在、现在也不存在任何西班牙当局来声明费雷尔先生无权印制护照。如果要提出投诉，必须由中国当局采取行动。

护照被退回

事情就此搁置。护照被退还给印刷公司。由于它们是依据费雷尔先生的授权订购的，因此是他的财产。

现在出现的问题是，是否任何西班牙公民都可以在上海印制护照并借此逃避逮捕。在一位西班牙公民看来，他们可以这样做，甚至可以实施任何犯罪行为而不必担心被依法逮捕。

If a Spanish citizen were to
commit anything short of murder
he would probably be able to
dodge arrest temporarily and in

ards with residence or domicile in

intolerable state of affairs," the
original complainant against the
printing of passports at the Eze-
chuen Road address has address-
ed a letter to Sir John Brenan,
senior member of the Consular
Body in Shanghai.
Facts Outlined
The first part of this letter out-
lines briefly the facts obtained by
police investigating his original
complaint; and goes on to say:
"Due to the fact that Spain
at present still enjoys the
privileges of extraterritoriality,
the S.M.P. can not seize this
printed matter and further-
more can not stop the activi-
ties of this bogus consul (re-
ferring to Ferrer). Your
Honor knows as well as I do
that these activities are irre-
gular and the person or per-
sons engaged in them are
committing an offence to the
legal government of Spain
and at the same time creating
the possibility of a disturbance
which may be prejudicial to
Settlement interests.
"Again I have to refer to
your Honor to the letter ad-
dressed by me to the French
Consul General, a copy of
which I sent to you on the
26th November 1936. I request
you once more to take up this
matter with your colleagues of
the Consular body and the
French authorities otherwise I
shall be compelled to take this
matter up with the Minister
of Foreign Affairs in Nanking
and request them to seize all
the archives, furnitures, seals
etc. pertaining to the Spanish
Government, which are at
present in the unlawful posses-
sion of Mr. Ferrer, being
aware of what may be the re-
sults
"Trusting that your Honor
will do the utmost in this
matter, I remain:
"Yours faithfully:"
Presents Problem
Up to the present, this letter
has not been answered, but it is
believed that a copy of it has
been sent to every consular re-
presentative in Shanghai.
What will come of the present
impasse remains a moot question,
but certain Spanish citizens are
now in communication with the
Spanish government at Valencia
(Loyalists) and letters have been
dispatched within the last two
days urgently requesting the
Valencia government to appoint a
representative in China or to
delegate consular powers to some
other country such as France.
French Concerned
While the present plight of the
Spanish community has been
called to the attention of the
French authorities here, it has
been intimated that they are un-
able to act without direct authori-
zation from Paris.
An answer is expected to reach
Shanghai from the Valencia go-
vernment within three weeks'
time, but if some solution of the
problem has not been found by
that time, a direct request will be
made to the Nanking government
to handle the situation as it sees
fit.

道奇能否逃避逮捕

如果一名西班牙公民犯下谋杀以外的任何罪行，他或许能够暂时逃避逮捕；而在谋杀案中，他可能会被拘留，以待就居住或定居在中国的西班牙人的地位问题作出决定。

原投诉人指责所谓“令人无法容忍的局势”，针对在四川路地址印制护照一事致函上海领事团资深成员约翰·布伦南爵士（Sir John Brenan）。

事实概要

该信第一部分简要概述了警方调查其原始投诉所获知的事实，并接着说道：

“鉴于西班牙目前仍享有治外法权特权，上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）无法扣押这些印刷品， furthermore 无法制止这位假冒领事（指费雷尔 Ferrer）的活动。阁下与我同样清楚，这些活动是不合规的，从事这些活动的人不仅对西班牙合法政府构成犯罪，同时也制造了可能损害租界利益的动荡隐患。

“此外，我不得不再次提请阁下注意我曾致法国总领事的信函，该信副本我已于1936年11月26日寄送给您。我再次请求您与领事团同仁及法国当局交涉此事，否则我将被迫向南京外交部提出此事，并请求他们扣押目前由费雷尔先生非法占有的所有属于西班牙政府的档案、家具、印章等物品，尽管我深知此举可能带来的后果。

“相信阁下将在此事上尽力而为，此致
敬礼：”

引发的问题

截至目前，这封信尚未收到回复，但据信其副本已发送给上海每一位领事代表。

目前的僵局将如何发展仍是一个悬而未决的问题，但某些西班牙公民现在正与瓦伦西亚的西班牙政府（忠诚派）联系，并在过去两天内发出信件，紧急请求瓦伦西亚政府任命一名驻华代表，或将领事权力委托给法国等其他国家。

法国方面的关切

虽然西班牙侨民目前的困境已提请注意驻沪法国当局，但据暗示，若无巴黎的直接授权，他们无法采取行动。

预计三周内将收到瓦伦西亚政府发给上海的答复，但如果届时仍未找到解决问题的办法，将直接向南京政府提出请求，由其酌情处理局势。

FEBRUARY 17, 1937.

Printing of Spanish Government Passports by the
Lee Hing Printing Coy., 533 Szechuen Road.

At 12 noon on February 16, 1937, Mr. J. Sanchez,
Spanish citizen, proprietor of the Shanghai Stucco Company,
505 Honan Road, was referred to D.S.I. Rhind by the P.A. to
D.C. (Crime) with a complaint that Spanish Passports were
being printed by the Lee Hing Printing Coy., 533 Szechuen
Road, without proper authority as the local Spanish Consulate-
General closed down some two months ago since when Spain has
not been represented in Shanghai by any duly accredited person.

From the Municipal Gazette dated September 11, 1936,
it will be seen that Dr. E. V. Ferrer resigned his post as
Consul-General for Spain sometime previous to that date and
that he was succeeded by the Acting Consul-General Mr. de
Larracechea. This latter official, however, left Shanghai
about two months ago without appointing a successor and as a
result the Consulate building in Avenue Joffre was closed
down.

In these circumstances, it appeared that Sanchez,
as a private Spanish citizen, had every right to make the
complaint he did provided his information as to the printing
of passports was in accordance with the facts. He assured
D.S.I. Rhind that he had actually visited the Lee Hing
(利興) Printing Company and had seen the passports for
himself, adding that these documents were being sold indis-
criminately to members of the public.

Accordingly, D.S.I. Rhind and D.S.I. [illegible],
accompanied by Sanchez, called at this shop and interviewed
one Mr. Tse Tsung Sheng (左宗盛) who [illegible]
the manager and part owner of the business. [illegible]

利兴印刷公司（Lee Hing Printing Coy.，四川路533号）印制西班牙政府护照事宜。

1937年2月16日中午12时，西班牙公民、河南路505号上海灰泥公司（Shanghai Stucco Company）业主J.桑切斯（J. Sanchez）先生，经警佐（P.A.）转介至刑事侦缉处副督察长（D.C. (Crime)）处的刑侦督察长（D.S.I.）林德（Rhind），投诉称利兴印刷公司（四川路533号）在无适当授权的情况下印制西班牙护照，因为当地西班牙总领事馆约于两个月前关闭，此后西班牙在上海没有任何正式认可的代表。

从1936年9月11日的《市政公报》（Municipal Gazette）可以看出，E. V. 费雷尔博士（Dr. E. V. Ferrer）在该日期之前的某个时候辞去了西班牙总领事职务，由代理总领事拉腊切恰先生（Mr. de Larracechea）继任。然而，这位官员约于两个月前离开上海，未任命继任者，导致霞飞路（Avenue Joffre）的领事馆大楼关闭。

在这种情况下，桑切斯作为一名普通西班牙公民，只要其关于护照印制的信息符合事实，便完全有权提出上述投诉。他向刑侦督察长林德保证，他确实访问了利兴（Lee Hing）印刷公司，并亲眼看到了护照，还补充说这些文件正 indiscriminately（不加甄别地/随意地）出售给公众。

因此，刑侦督察长林德和刑侦督察长[原文不清]，在桑切斯的陪同下，前往该店，会见了谢宗盛（Tse Tsung Sheng，音译：左宗盛）先生，他是该业务的经理兼部分所有者。[原文不清]

毫不迟疑地透露，就在去年2月7日，一位维森西诺维奇先生（Mr. Vesensinovich）以西班牙总领事馆的名义下达了一份订单，订购：(1) 50本西班牙护照，以及 (2) 100张印有“西班牙总领事馆”抬头并盖有西班牙合法政府印章印模的信笺。他表示这些物品已经印制完毕，他正等待客户回来付款并提货。事实上，作为证明，他展示了这些物品已被打包成两个包裹，放在店里的柜台上。其中一个包裹上附有一张开给维森西诺维奇先生、转交西班牙领事馆（c/o Spanish Consulate）的账单，其中列明了物品及收费价格，总计7.50美元。

值得注意的是，西班牙合法政府的印章压印在护照封面上。对此，经理表示，印刷厂内有几枚印章，这些是公司的财产，是根据领事馆大约五六年前提供的设计制作的。他指出，该公司在过去十年里一直承担领事馆的各种印刷业务。如果就目前印制此类物品的合法性产生任何疑问，他表示愿意将印版、护照和信笺移交给警方。

在下署人和朱刑侦督察长（D.S.I. Chu）访问该店期间，未发现任何证据表明护照正在向公众出售。事实上，该店及其人员享有良好的正派声誉，桑切斯所称护照被随意出售的说法毫无根据。

完成这些查询后，刑侦督察长林德致电V. 维森齐诺维奇先生（Mr. V. Vesenzinovich），在谈话中得知，他是应E. V. 费雷尔博士的要求下达该订单的，他承认费雷尔博士为现任总领事。他解释说自己担任领事馆随员（Chancellor）一职已有数年；这确属事实。

随后，刑侦督察长林德致电费雷尔博士位于国泰公寓（Cathay Mansions）的住所，费雷尔博士坦承这些物品和护照是应他的要求订购的。他表示，他现在是西班牙“国民”政府（National ' Government）的总领事，打算向希望返回西班牙的人士签发护照。向他解释说，警方介入此事是由于桑切斯（Sanches）提出的投诉，后者声称目前上海没有西班牙总领事或授权代表。听到这一点后，他将桑切斯描述为一个骗子和欺诈者，此人曾多次引起租界警方和法国警方的注意，并建议完全忽略来自他的任何投诉。

最后，下署人与桑切斯一同去见市政检察官（Municipal Advocate）以寻求建议。由于桑切斯质疑费雷尔博士作为总领事行事的权限，市政检察官请来了领事团秘书希尔先生（Mr. Hill），在与他协商后得出结论：警方在此事上无法采取行动。他补充说，虽然可以向特区法院（S.S.D. Court）申请没收护照等物品，但采取这一途径并不明智，因为这可能会危及西班牙在华的治外法权。希尔先生承诺将此
